newsitem.title: USA: Jury deliberates in Carroll O'Connor slander case.
newsitem.headline: Jury deliberates in Carroll O'Connor slander case.

text.p: Jurors deliberated all day Thursday without reaching a verdict in the slander lawsuit brought against actor Carroll O'Connor by a man he blamed for his son's suicide.

The jury of six men and six women was instructed by County Court Judge Malcolm Mackey that, to find in favour of the plaintiff, they would have to conclude O'Connor's public statements amounted to "despicable conduct."
Such conduct, the judge said, would be "so vile, base, contemptible, miserable, wretched and loathsome that it would be looked down upon and despised by ordinary decent people."

Harry Perzigian, who was jailed in 1996 for drug possession, sued the 72-year-old O'Connor for unspecified damages for his comments. O'Connor claimed Perzigian supplied cocaine to his son, Hugh, who shot himself in March 1995.
After seven days of testimony in the civil trial, the jury was handed the case Thursday morning. A majority of nine is sufficient to reach a verdict either way.

In one TV interview, the actor, who played the opinionated Archie Bunker in "All in the Family" and a southern police chief in "In the Heat of the Night," called Perzigian "a partner in murder" and in another, he called him "a lawbreaker." He also gave out Perzigian's address and showed his photo.

Perzigian, who is seeking damages for slander and emotional distress, argued he was in fear of his life after O'Connor said in other TV interviews: "Harry Perzigian, you sleaze-ball. We're going to get you" and "I want to hurt him in the worst way."
O'Connor said the "partner in murder" quote was a figure of speech and no reasonable listener would believe he was accusing Perzigian of murder. In any case, there was no murder, he said.
Also he said he did not mean physical harm to Perzigian when he spoke of harming him. Rather, he merely meant to expose him as a drug dealer.
